claim_ceiling: REPRODUCED tier for the corrected legal-distance state. FALSIFIED (as accepted): 'dense multilingual-e5 embeddings RECOVER citation heritage at scale (AUC 0.79-0.85) BETTER than TF-IDF citation (AUC 0.71-0.74)'. On identical matched self-pair-free ORIG pairs dense_cp64 = 0.7189 vs cited_decisions_tfidf = 0.7159 (margin +0.0030 < pre-registered +0.02; 2000-resample bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0343,+0.0366]); the gap was a pair-set mismatch (dense 730 vs TF-IDF 1020) plus 174/1020 degenerate (d,d) self-pairs inflating every representation by ~0.045-0.051 AUC. Verified by independent raw-input recomputation (exact to float noise). SURVIVING (qualified): dense embeddings CARRY citation-relatedness signal (0.719 ORIG no-self cp64; 0.69 DIRECT; 0.92-0.97 shared-citation) and are justified ONLY as a text-only proxy when citation metadata is absent; with resolved citations the full-dim binary citation Jaccard is stronger (0.7735 DIRECT / 1.000 SHARED2 vs dense 0.6924 / 0.9698). 'AUC > 0.75 PASSED' is pair-set dependent (ORIG no-self 0.7189 FAILS; FULL no-self 0.9176 PASSES) and must never be quoted unqualified. UNCHANGED accepted findings: section cross-lingual hierarchy at 1K (Sachverhalt 0.282>0.2, Dispositiv 0.150>0.1, Erwaegungen 0.094<0.1); linear-hybrid complement passes adversarial but JP 0.61-0.67 < TF-IDF 0.78-0.79 (not primary); dense fails jurist gate at all scales; two-mode tradeoff fundamental. No new claims. Data blockers unchanged (bge_/bger_ mapping, parquet 2024-2026, 174k section extraction).
